the_single_most_important_measurement_of.meaning: the demonstration compiles, the skill transfers to a database it has never seen in four milliseconds, and the door the model is actually used through never asks for it. The capability existed and was unreachable.

the_three_bugs__all_in_the_compiler_neve.bug: substitution rewrote values inside hole names
the_three_bugs__all_in_the_compiler_neve.evidence: the literal demonstration `UPDATE items SET qty = 40 WHERE id = 1` compiled to `UPDATE items SET qty = ?num?num0 WHERE id = ?num0`
the_three_bugs__all_in_the_compiler_neve.cause: _substitute_in_obj called out.replace(raw_val, hole) with no shielding, so the value '1' matched the '1' inside the hole '?num0'
the_three_bugs__all_in_the_compiler_neve.fix: shield every hole already present with a sentinel before substituting; restore after. Bare numbers now match whole tokens only, so '1' no longer eats the 1 in '12'.
the_three_bugs__all_in_the_compiler_neve.severity: produced unparseable SQL -- any demonstration whose values shared a digit with a hole name was uncompilable

the_three_bugs__all_in_the_compiler_neve.bug: the twin-world synthesiser could not replay bound parameters
the_three_bugs__all_in_the_compiler_neve.evidence: learn on `UPDATE items SET qty = ? WHERE id = ?` with params [40,1] failed with heldout_reason POSTCONDITION_SQLITE_NO_ROW
the_three_bugs__all_in_the_compiler_neve.cause: every `?` consumed params[0], and `?` in the WHERE clause was skipped entirely, so the twin row was seeded with the wrong key and the held-out postcondition found no row
the_three_bugs__all_in_the_compiler_neve.fix: bound parameters are consumed in appearance order across SET and WHERE, via a single cursor
the_three_bugs__all_in_the_compiler_neve.severity: THE PREFERRED OUTPUT SHAPE OF THE COMPILER COULD NEVER QUALIFY. The compiler emits bound `?` parameters; the gate that decides whether a skill may be learned could not replay them. Every parameterized SQLite skill was permanently unlearnable.

the_three_bugs__all_in_the_compiler_neve.bug: recall raised instead of refusing on a shape mismatch
the_three_bugs__all_in_the_compiler_neve.evidence: a skill compiled against table `items` matched the goal 'set id 1 to 77 in other.sqlite' and raised sqlite3.OperationalError: no such table: items out of the caller
the_three_bugs__all_in_the_compiler_neve.cause: execute_compiled_steps was called unguarded inside the candidate loop
the_three_bugs__all_in_the_compiler_neve.fix: a step failure is a candidate miss, not an exception; the loop continues to the next candidate and the door keeps the real reason
the_three_bugs__all_in_the_compiler_neve.severity: an exception at the door became COMPOSER_STEP_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN, which names no cause

what_now_works_end_to_end_and_was_verifi.negative_control: the same skill does NOT transfer to a database with a different table -- it refuses rather than raising

the_deliberate_refusal_i_did_NOT_overrid.code: closed_loop_autonomous_controller_v1.py line 589: recalled = None if (not learn or computer_shape) else recall_and_execute_workflow(...)
the_deliberate_refusal_i_did_NOT_overrid.measured: computer_shape is True for 'set id 1 to 40 in x.sqlite', 'compress logs into bundle.tar.gz', and 'how many unique lines in data.txt'. It is False for 'rename calc.py to main.py'.
the_deliberate_refusal_i_did_NOT_overrid.why_it_exists: a learned skill is EVIDENCE of what was done before; it is not AUTHORITY to act now. Computer-shaped actions need an admitted confinement and a verification path before they may run.
the_deliberate_refusal_i_did_NOT_overrid.why_i_did_not_remove_it: removing a fail-closed confinement gate to make a demo pass is exactly the corruption this project legislates against. The gate is correct; what is missing is the admitted confinement it is waiting for.
the_deliberate_refusal_i_did_NOT_overrid.the_cheapest_heal: if this machine has a separate workspace directory and an operator consents, that operator's once-per-session authorization supplies exactly the 'admitted confinement' the refusal names -- and the confinement evidence for each execution is the skill's own postcondition check, which is deterministic. Do not build a self-declared flag; that makes the refusal into a formality.

connection_to_round_25: round 25 gave the oracle five semantic UI postcondition kinds because it could not see a GUI. This round shows the same problem one layer down: for computer-shaped goals the door never reaches recall at all, so no oracle is consulted. A verifier that is never called has the same effect as a verifier that does not exist.

what_this_proves_and_what_it_does_not.proves: the same skill, learned from one demonstration, reaches a database it has never seen in ~4 ms and writes the correct value, for both shapes the compiler emits.
does_NOT_prove: that the door will use it on this machine -- it will not, and that is a deliberate refusal standing exactly where the claim needs it to be absent
that this generalises to coding. The coding rate remains 1 of 9 unique bugs = 11.1%

that the skill is the RIGHT skill. The permanence finding from round 24 is untouched: one demonstration still selects among several consistent rules, and the held-out + sabotage gate is what makes the selection safe
anything about computer use beyond the semantic oracle built in round 25 -- still zero terminal results on a real desktop
